title: Quarter activation blueprint: Private/VPC & on-prem orchestration
creator: Aisha R. Patel
description: Purpose: Produce a prescriptive quarter-level activation blueprint that ties Private/VPC/on‑prem feature deliverables to measurable OKRs, release gates, and customer cohorts. This ticket synthesizes engineering capacity, security constraints, and partner onboarding windows into a single playbook for Q2 activation and handoff to Customer Success. Outcome: a published playbook + sprint-aligned milestone plan, clear acceptance gates, and a mapping of features -> OKRs -> rollout cohorts.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc (Confluence) published and reviewed by Eng, Security, and CS with signoff from PM leads
All Q2 features assigned owners and sprint buckets in JIRA/Linear with estimates and dependencies annotated
Gate checklist created for private activation (networking, KMS, audit logs, upgrade path) and validated in staging
Customer cohort mapping exported and validated with GTM (at least 3 anchor customers identified for first tranche)
Risk & rollback runbook included with incident contact matrix and SLA impact assessment
milestones: 2026-03-05: Draft playbook outline and working doc created
2026-03-17: Finalize gating checklist and release criteria
2026-03-24: Sprint bucket assignments and dependencies locked
2026-03-31: Publish playbook and present to leadership; open readiness alpha cohort
comments: 2026-03-02 | Aisha R. Patel: Initial draft ready; flagged IP network sizing as potential pinch point. Asked Eng to validate kernel/throughput assumptions for isolated tenants.
2026-03-04 | Diego M. Santos: Eng review - confirmed autoscaling hook work is scheduled in ENG-1842 but needs API contract; opened ENG-7682 to spec contract between runtime and tenancy-controller.

decisions: Adopt tranche-based activation (Tranche 1: small pilot tenants; Tranche 2: medium production; Tranche 3: broad rollout)
Require KMS integration and audit log stream before any customer is activated in Tranche 1
Use existing dedicated capacity autoscaling primitives rather than building a bespoke scheduler for this quarter (trade-off: faster go-to-market vs fine-grained cost optimization)
risks: HSM/KMS vendor onboarding delays pushing readiness by 3+ weeks
Network egress/topology constraints for on-prem customers increase SRE overhead
Unforeseen incompatibility between runtime quantized kernels and customer-specific models leading to performance regressions
mitigations: Start parallel vendor onboarding for top-2 HSM options; negotiate provisional test credentials
Build a simplified VPN testing harness for early network validation with CS before full activation
Create a 'runtime-compatibility' test suite and run against customer model artifacts during sandbox sign-up
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Alpha cohort (2 anchor customers, limited feature set)
Phase 2 - Expand cohort (10 customers, add autoscaling and upgrade testing)
Phase 3 - General availability (wider GTM enablement, expanded docs and runbooks)
notes: This playbook should be consumable as a one‑pager for execs and a 20‑page runbook for operators.
Coordinate with Console team for a temporary dashboard tile that surfaces tranche readiness signals (token throughput, KMS status, audit-event lag).
Recommend a brownout test scheduled in Week 2 of Tranche 2 to validate rollback semantics and fallbacks to hosted variants.
